chunks.text: Summer Sprint Plan May 11 – June 30, 2026 • 51 Days How to Use This Plan This plan is designed to be tough but humane. Read this section once, then return to it when you feel overwhelmed. The Six Tracks DSA — 2 hours daily, every working day. No exceptions. This is the foundation. MegaProject (Anisight) — Targeted blocks, due by June 7. MERN (concepts + projects) — Daily focus until June 20. AWS Certification — Daily focus until June 15 (then exam). Open Source — 3-4 days/week, light commitment per day. Communication — 30 minutes daily, every working day. Tiny dose, huge compounding effect. Rest Schedule (NON-NEGOTIABLE) Sundays = Full rest. No DSA, no projects. Recover. Wednesdays = Half day. DSA + one light task only. Done by 1 PM. This gives you ~14 recovery days across 51. That's the difference between finishing strong and burning out in week 4. Anti-Burnout Rules If you miss a day, do NOT try to make it up by doubling tomorrow. Just continue. Hard stop at 7:30 PM. After that, you are off duty. Phone away from study desk. Pomodoro inside each block: 50 min work, 10 min break. Don't grind for 2 hours straight. If a problem/concept blocks you for 45+ min, flag it and move on. Return tomorrow. Sleep 7+ hours. This is part of the plan, not optional. DSA performance dies without sleep. Why This Sequence AWS exam is your earliest hard deadline (June 15), so it gets heavy weight in the first 4 weeks. MERN runs in parallel because the two complement each other (you'll deploy MERN apps to AWS). MegaProject ramps up in late May once you have foundations. DSA never stops because that's how skill is built — daily reps for 51 days. Track-by-Track Breakdown Track 1: DSA (No Leniency) You said you're below-medium to barely-medium. Plan: build mastery by topic, not by random problem-solving. 2 hours daily, structured. Daily structure (2 hours): First 30 min: Read/watch concept theory for current topic (use Striver's SDE sheet, NeetCode roadmap, or takeUforward). Next 75 min: Solve 2-3 problems on that topic. Start easy, end medium. Last 15 min: Write notes — pattern, complexity, mistake you made. This is what makes it stick. Topic schedule across 7 weeks: Week 1 (May 11-17): Arrays + Strings — fundamentals, two-pointer basics Week 2 (May 18-24): Hashing + Sliding Window Week 3 (May 25-31): Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists Week 4 (Jun 1-7): Recursion + Backtracking (this is where most people get stuck — go slow) Week 5 (Jun 8-14): Trees (BT + BST traversals, problems) Week 6 (Jun 15-21): Dynamic Programming (1D, 2D, classic problems) Week 7 (Jun 22-30): Graphs (BFS, DFS, shortest path) + revision of weak topics Weekly target: 12-15 problems solved with full understanding. Quality > quantity. Re-solving a problem from scratch the next week is more valuable than 5 new problems half-understood. Approach: ship in milestones, not in one big push. Week 1-2 (May 11-24): Planning, architecture, tech stack lock-in, base setup. ~1 hr/day. Week 3-4 (May 25-Jun 7): MAIN BUILD PHASE. ~3 hrs/day. This is when MegaProject gets your primary block. June 8-10: Buffer for polish, deployment, README, demo video. Make a feature checklist on Day 1. Cross things off. Don't add scope mid-way. Track 3: MERN Stack Deadline: June 20. Concepts + projects (multiple, not one giant one). May 11-17: MongoDB + Mongoose deep dive. Mini-project: CRUD API. May 18-24: Express.js + REST principles + auth (JWT). Mini-project: Auth-protected blog API. May 25-31: React fundamentals + hooks + state management. Mini-project: Frontend for blog API. Jun 1-7: React advanced (context, custom hooks, routing). Mini-project: Multi-page app. Jun 8-14: Full MERN integration. Mini-project: Full-stack todo or notes app with auth. Jun 15-20: Polish 1-2 projects to portfolio quality. Deploy them (use AWS skills here). Track 4: AWS Certification Deadline: June 15. Recommended cert for first-timers: AWS Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02). If you're aiming for Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03), the same plan works but problems get harder. Week 1-2 (May 11-24): Core services — EC2, S3, IAM, VPC basics. Watch Stephane Maarek or Adrian Cantrill course. Week 3 (May 25-31): Databases (RDS, DynamoDB), Lambda, networking deeper. Week 4 (Jun 1-7): Security, monitoring, billing, well-architected framework. Start practice tests. Jun 8-14: PRACTICE TESTS DAILY. Tutorials Dojo or Whizlabs. Aim for 80%+ before booking exam. Jun 15: Take the exam. Or earlier if you hit 85% on practice tests by Jun 12. Track 5: Open Source 3-4 days/week, ~1 hour each. Goal is consistent contribution, not heroic PRs. Pick 2-3 active beginner-friendly repos in week 1 (look for 'good first issue' label). Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri: 1 hour each. Read code, comment on issues, submit small PRs. Skip on Wednesday (half day) and weekends if tired. Don't force it. Realistic 7-week target: 4-8 merged PRs. Quality of contribution > number. Track 6: Communication & Interview Communication 30 minutes daily, weekdays only. This is the highest-ROI track for placements/interviews. Recommended weekly curriculum: Monday — Read aloud (10 min) + record yourself explaining one DSA concept (20 min). Listen back. Tuesday — Mock behavioral question. Use STAR method. Record + review. Wednesday — (half day, skip if tired) Listen to one tech talk/podcast, take notes. Thursday — Mock technical question: explain a project or DSA solution out loud as if to interviewer. Friday — Vocab + filler-word audit. Practice eliminating 'um', 'like', 'basically'. Resources: Pramp (free mock interviews — try once a week if possible), YouTube channels like Clément Mihailescu, IGotAnOffer. Standard Daily Templates These are your default schedules. Standard Weekday (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat) Half Day (Wednesday) Rest Day (Sunday) Week 1: May 11 – May 17 Theme: Foundations. Set up everything. DSA = Arrays/Strings. Begin AWS, MERN (Mongo), MegaProject planning. Week 2: May 18 – May 24 Theme: Backend depth. DSA = Hashing + Sliding Window. AWS gets denser. Express + Auth in MERN. Week 3: May 25 – May 31 Theme: MegaProject ramp-up + Frontend begins. DSA = Stacks/Queues/LL. AWS = Databases + Lambda. Week 4: June 1 – June 7 Theme: MegaProject final push + AWS exam prep heavy. DSA = Recursion/Backtracking (the hardest topic — go slow). Week 5: June 8 – June 14 Theme: AWS exam home stretch. DSA = Trees. MERN = Full integration. MegaProject DONE — don't touch it. Week 6: June 15 – June 21 Theme: AWS exam day + post-exam recovery. DSA = DP (the second hardest topic). MERN finishes by June 20. Week 7: June 22 – June 30 Theme: Graphs + revision + portfolio polish. The home stretch. DSA only and revision of weak topics. Weekly Review Template (Sundays — Optional) Spend 30 min Sunday morning answering these. The rest of the day is fully off. DSA: How many problems solved? Which topic was weakest? What pattern repeated? AWS / MERN / MegaProject: % progress vs plan? On track, ahead, behind? Communication: Did I record myself this week? What's one filler word I overuse? Open Source: PRs opened, merged, in review? Energy: Did I sleep 7+ hrs/night? Skip any rest days? (If yes, that's a problem.) Adjust: What ONE thing am I changing next week? Final Note This plan is ambitious. Not everything will go perfectly — that's expected, not a failure. The goal is to finish June 30 with: 100+ DSA problems solved across all major topics, AWS cert in hand, a finished MegaProject, 2-3 polished MERN projects deployed, 4-8 open-source PRs merged, and noticeably better communication on camera. If you hit 75% of that, you've had a transformative summer. Trust the rest days. Show up daily. Don't grind past 7:30 PM. You've got this.
